 Follow Russia says responding to US report of planned attack on Moscow
 AFP Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:07 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The Tsaritsyno museum is an imperial palace and park complex in southern Moscow (Mladen ANTONOV) Russia's FSB security service said on Saturday it was carrying out "appropriate" measures after the US embassy in Moscow warned of a planned "terrorist" attack in the capital.
 The US embassy said earlier it was "aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow".
 The US government was "coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response," it said, advising people: "Avoid the area, stay alert, and avoid crowds."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The US embassy did not give details on who was plotting the attack.
 The Tsaritsyno museum is an imperial palace and park complex in southern Moscow that is a popular place to visit, especially on weekends.
 Russian Telegram channel Baza, which reportedly has links to law enforcement, said the park was now closed and "open only for exits".
 "Law enforcement officers are on the premises," it reported.
 Russia's FSB security service said earlier it had received information from the United States "regarding the preparation of a terrorist attack".
 "Appropriate work is underway," it was quoted as saying by Russian news agencies.
 The US has provided Russia with warnings of planned attacks before, including in March 2024, weeks before an ISIS-K attack on a Moscow concert hall that killed over 100 people.
